currentManifestItem.title: A fixed Cartesian polarization is not a global transverse helicity frame

references.title: Eric Palmerduca and Hong Qin, Photon topology, arXiv:2308.11147v2
Konstantin Y. Bliokh, Miguel A. Alonso, Elena A. Ostrovskaya, and Andrea Aiello, Angular Momenta and Spin-Orbit Interaction of Nonparaxial Light in Free Space
David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6, section 6.2.1

currentManifestItem.statement: Let $e_1,e_2,e_3$ be the standard coordinate basis of $\mathbb R^3$. The constant Cartesian circular vectors $e_\sigma^0=(e_1+i\sigma e_2)/\sqrt2$, for $\sigma=\pm1$, form a transverse helicity frame for every nonzero momentum direction; consequently this fixed pair supplies a momentum-independent polarization factor on the transverse one-photon space.
